text:
ila: quick brain dump — we've been seeing high slab churn from lots of micro-prefixes. what if instead of a fixed namespace bucket we do adaptive micro-bucketing: bucket cold prefixes by temporal inactivity and attachment size, then apply a soft-demote with hysteresis?
yves: can you sketch the hysteresis? curious how we avoid oscillation if a prefix flares briefly and then quiets again.
ila: idea: each prefix has a tiny score window (decay-based). if score < throttle_thresh for X minutes -> candidate for packing. packing groups prefixes into a micro-bucket. demote only after bucket-level grace window (G) and only if revived ratio < revive_threshold in that window.
kamal: this sounds promising. two immediate questions: 1) how do we preserve read-after-write for long-running cursors? 2) how do we handle leases and credits?
anya: for RW we should never remove prefix-level metadata for prefixes that have outstanding prefix-leases/cursors. packing only considers prefixes with no active prefix-lease. that keeps semantics intact.
sre-tiger: for leases/credits we could maintain a bucket-lease (cheap) and keep prefix-lease for in-flight ops. bucket-lease manages eviction credit accounting while prefix-lease gates cursor visibility.
ila: exactly. another angle: soft-demote vs hard-evict. soft-demote marks a bucket as "cold-packed" but keeps a lightweight tombstone in slab directory so a single write can rehydrate quickly, avoiding full fetch.
yves: what about cross-node consistency? if we pack locally but not globally, reads from other nodes might not find prefix manifest. need a manifest replication or a cheap consensus hint.
kamal: cheap approach: publish bucket manifests to a small consistent kv (etcd) with epoch ids. demote is two-phase: 1) write manifest+epoch 2) wait for manifest ack from local replicas 3) flip demote bit. reads check manifest epoch and consult primary if miss.
anya: downside: extra round-trip. To minimize: only publish for buckets that cross a node boundary (multi-affinity). single-node buckets use local mem manifest.
sre-tiger: telemetry: collect pack_rate, demote_rate, revive_count, bucket_revive_ratio, cold_read_latency, rehydrate_latency. also tag by tenant.
ila: we should instrument a new metric: bucket_revival_burst = count(prefixes revived within 60s after demote). set soft alarm at 10/min per tenant.
yves: tests: simulation harness to create tens of thousands micro-prefixes with Poisson traffic and then run the packer to validate revive_ratio and average demote ops. unit tests: manifest pub/sub failure modes.
kamal: implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
# pack decision (run periodically)
for prefix in namespace.candidate_prefixes():
    if prefix.score < throttle_thresh and not prefix.has_prefix_lease():
        add_to_bucket(prefix, bucket_key_for(prefix))

def bucket_key_for(prefix):
    # deterministic but adaptive: hash + size class + inactivity window id
    return f"{ns}:{hash(prefix)%128}:{size_class(prefix)}:{window_id}"
```

anya: adaptive bucket_key keeps hot tiny prefixes from getting noisy buckets. if a tiny prefix becomes hot we promote it out immediately.
sre-tiger: fallback policy: if bucket_revive_ratio > 0.25 for a tenant over a 1h window - auto-disable packing for that tenant.
ila: rollout plan: enable packing only for tenants with < 50 active prefixes and average prefix qps < 0.2 for 24h. run for 72h, compare baseline for cold-miss and demote_ops. start in staging on 0.5% traffic.
yves: corner-case: backlog replay after a node restart could see manifests lagging and accidentally double-fetch. solution: demote epoch numbering + idempotent rehydrate which ignores duplicate inflight fetches.
kamal: ops: add console dashboard called "packed-prefix churn" with tiles: bucket_count, avg_prefixes_per_bucket, bucket_revival_burst, per-tenant auto-disable.
anya: security note: ensure bucket manifests don't leak prefixes across namespaces; always namespace-prefix the manifest key and validate on read.
sre-tiger: would like a canary test that injects a hot-surge workload after demote to ensure promotion latency < 50ms median.
ops-bot: created INF-4201: "adaptive micro-bucketing prototype + canary" assigned to @ila, @kamal. canary: staging 0.5% tenants, ga gate: revive_ratio < 0.1 AND p99_cold_read < baseline*1.15 for 72h.
ila: ok i'll prototype packer + epoched manifest write. @yves can you own the simulation harness? @anya add manifest validation tests. we'll re-check in 1 week. :thumbsup:
